title: Social Interactions: Being A Likeable Boss
overview: Effective leadership is shaped not only by authority, expertise, and decision-making ability, but also by the quality of the relationships a manager builds with people. Employees are more willing to communicate openly, cooperate, accept feedback, and contribute discretionary effort when they experience their manager as approachable, fair, respectful, trustworthy, and genuinely interested in their success.

This course develops the interpersonal and social skills required to become a respected and likeable boss without sacrificing accountability, standards, or managerial authority. Participants explore how leadership behavior influences trust, engagement, psychological safety, motivation, and team relationships, and how everyday interactions can strengthen or weaken a manager's credibility.

The program focuses on practical behaviors such as listening, empathy, recognition, constructive communication, fairness, accessibility, emotional self-management, feedback, conflict handling, and maintaining appropriate professional boundaries. Through self-assessment, workplace scenarios, role plays, discussions, and practical exercises, participants will develop an individual leadership interaction plan for building stronger relationships while maintaining performance expectations.
audience: Managers, supervisors, team leaders, section heads, project leaders, newly appointed managers, and professionals who lead or coordinate the work of others and wish to strengthen their interpersonal effectiveness, employee relationships, and leadership presence.
methodology: This course uses an interactive, behavior-focused methodology combining short facilitator inputs with self-assessments, leadership reflection exercises, case studies, group discussions, role plays, workplace scenarios, communication practice, feedback exercises, and action planning. Participants will examine realistic managerial situations involving trust, recognition, feedback, difficult conversations, conflict, boundaries, and employee motivation. Practical activities will allow participants to experiment with alternative leadership responses and receive structured feedback on their interpersonal impact.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain how everyday managerial behavior influences trust, engagement, cooperation, and employee perceptions.
Assess their current interpersonal leadership style and identify behaviors that strengthen or weaken relationships.
Build credibility through consistency, fairness, respect, reliability, and appropriate transparency.
Use active listening, empathy, and effective questioning to understand employees more accurately.
Communicate expectations, decisions, and feedback in a clear, respectful, and constructive manner.
Demonstrate appreciation and recognition in ways that support motivation and performance.
Balance approachability and friendliness with authority, accountability, and professional boundaries.
Manage disagreement, tension, and difficult conversations without damaging working relationships.
Adapt their interaction style to different personalities, situations, and employee needs.
Develop a practical action plan for becoming a more trusted, respected, and positively influential manager.
